page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on a KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance includes 128.0 GB of memory, equating to a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio (8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU). It does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, meaning all persistent data relies on attached network storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across parallel tasks, tempered by modest single-threaded throughput. In Geekbench testing, the instance scores 1317.0 for single-core and 7366.0 for multi-core processing, while PassMark registers an overall CPU score of 19092.02. CPU-heavy synthetic stress testing aligns with this pattern, reporting a stress-ng multi-core score of 6113.37 alongside a bottom-decile single-core score of 763.49. In-memory data workloads show robust capability, logging 14.27 million Redis SET operations per second and 742.7 GB/sec in cached small-block memory reads. However, uncached 256 MB memory transfers decrease to 29.99 GB/sec for reads and 15.38 GB/sec for writes.

The hardware configuration of ecs.r6a.4xlarge prioritizes memory capacity over compute intensity or ultra-fast storage input/output. It is well-suited for enterprise in-memory caches, relational database systems, large-footprint Java or JVM applications, and general data analysis workloads that fit entirely into system memory without requiring local scratch NVMe disks.

The instance lacks local storage and hardware GPU accelerators, relying on remote volumes and providing a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Its performance profile reflects stable multi-threaded execution and high memory capacity, highlighted by 14.27 million Redis SET operations per second and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7366.0, despite weaker single-thread stress-ng scores (763.49) and modest uncached memory throughput. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio positions it effectively for memory-heavy enterprise workloads, including in-memory databases, Redis deployments, and large caching layers.
